title: Muon: An Optimizer for Hidden Layers
hook: Muon orthogonalizes each gradient update before applying it — and trained networks faster than AdamW, the first serious challenger to Adam's reign in years.
key_points: Optimizes 2D hidden-layer weight matrices by orthogonalizing the momentum update.
Uses a cheap Newton–Schulz iteration to approximate the nearest orthogonal matrix.
Set speed records on nanoGPT and CIFAR training 'speedruns' over tuned AdamW.
Pairs with a standard optimizer (e.g. AdamW) for embeddings and 1D parameters.
content_html: Muon is an optimizer introduced by Keller Jordan in late 2024 that targets the weight matrices of a network's hidden layers. Where Adam and AdamW rescale each parameter independently, Muon treats a layer's update as a matrix and replaces it with the nearest orthogonal matrix before applying it — and in practice this trains networks measurably faster.
extra_html:
How it works

Muon takes the momentum update that ordinary SGD-with-momentum would apply, then "orthogonalizes" it using a few steps of the Newton–Schulz iteration — a cheap way to approximate the nearest orthogonal matrix without a full singular value decomposition. Intuitively this prevents the update from collapsing into a few dominant directions, spreading learning more evenly across the layer. Muon is applied only to 2D hidden weights; embeddings, the final layer, and 1D parameters are left to a conventional optimizer like AdamW.

Why it matters

Adam and AdamW have been the default for so long that a genuinely faster optimizer is news. Muon first proved itself on community training "speedruns" — reaching a target loss in fewer steps than heavily tuned AdamW — and the idea has since drawn serious attention for scaling up. It is a reminder that the optimizer, not just the architecture, is still fertile ground for efficiency gains.

related.title: AdamW: Decoupled Weight Decay
related.hook: L2 regularization and weight decay are the same thing for plain SGD - but not for Adam. Decoupling them fixes Adam's generalization and makes the best decay value independent of the learning rate.

related.title: Adam: The Default Optimizer
related.hook: Adam gives every parameter its own adaptive step size by tracking the gradient's recent average and spread — and it mostly just works.

related.title: Learning Rate & Schedules
related.hook: The single most important hyperparameter: set it too high and training diverges, too low and it crawls — so we warm it up, then decay it.

flashcards.back_html: It treats the momentum update as a matrix and replaces it with the nearest orthogonal matrix (via a cheap Newton–Schulz iteration), rather than rescaling each parameter independently.

choices.text: To stop the update collapsing into a few dominant directions, spreading learning across the layer
To shrink the weights for regularization
To compress the gradient for lower memory
